questions.question: A 'while' loop in Python will continue to execute as long as its condition is True.
The 'for' loop in Python always requires an explicit increment step specified by the user.
The 'break' statement can immediately terminate a loop without checking the loop's condition.
In Python, you can only iterate over lists using a 'for' loop.
The 'continue' statement in Python skips the rest of the code inside a loop for the current iteration and continues with the next iteration of the loop.
Nested loops allow you to iterate over a sequence while another sequence is being iterated.
A 'for' loop can iterate directly over the keys of a dictionary.
Using an else clause with loops in Python will execute the else block only if the loop was not terminated by a 'break' statement.
In Python, 'range(5)' produces the sequence that includes the number 5.
It is not possible to have an infinite loop in Python if there is a logical error in the loop condition.
